The Education

Why Acupuncture Billing Has the Most Inconsistent Coverage Landscape

Acupuncture billing is the process of coding and submitting insurance claims for acupuncture services to the payers that cover them and correctly identifying and separately invoicing the payers that do not. Unlike most specialties where coverage policies are relatively uniform, acupuncture coverage varies by payer, by plan, by indication, by state, and sometimes by the specific employer group plan creating a payer landscape that requires constant verification before every patient encounter.

Medicare's 2020 expansion of acupuncture coverage for chronic low back pain is the most significant acupuncture billing development in U.S. history. Medicare now covers up to 12 acupuncture sessions in 90 days for Medicare beneficiaries with chronic low back pain with up to 8 additional sessions for patients showing improvement. The coverage applies to licensed acupuncturists, physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants. Correctly billing Medicare for CLBP requires the correct CPT codes (97810-97814), correct diagnosis (M54.5 or M54.50-M54.59), the correct session count tracking, and documentation of improvement when billing additional sessions.

Dry needling performed by physical therapists and some physicians is billed differently from acupuncture. Dry needling uses physical therapy procedure codes (97140 manual therapy, sometimes 97810-97814 in states where PT acupuncture codes are permitted) rather than acupuncture-specific codes. When an acupuncturist and a PT perform both services to the same patient, PMEx ensures each service is coded under the correct provider and code set.

The Widest Coverage Inconsistency of Any Specialty in U.S. Medicine

The Medicare Coverage vs. Commercial Payer Inconsistency Map

Medicare covers acupuncture for chronic low back pain. Some commercial plans cover acupuncture broadly. Others cover it for specific indications only. Many cover it with prior authorization. Some cover it as an out-of-network-only benefit. Some employer group plans exclude it entirely while other plans from the same carrier cover it. State Medicaid programs vary even more dramatically California Medi-Cal covers acupuncture, while most state Medicaid programs do not.

The most expensive mistake in acupuncture billing is submitting to a payer that does not cover the service the claim is denied, the patient was never informed of self-pay obligation, and the revenue is permanently lost. The second most expensive mistake is routing a covered service to self-pay billing a patient $120 out of pocket for a visit their UnitedHealthcare plan covers at $65 copay. Both errors erode practice revenue and patient trust simultaneously.

PMEx runs eligibility verification and acupuncture coverage confirmation for every patient before every appointment routing covered services to the correct insurance plan with correct authorization, and informing patients of self-pay obligations before non-covered services are delivered.

Wrong Dx Code

Acupuncture Claim Denied for Incorrect Diagnosis Code

Chronic low back pain billed with non-specific back pain code M54.5 when M54.50 (vertebrogenic, unspecified) would have been more specific and avoided medical necessity review.

PMEx applies the most specific ICD-10 code for each acupuncture indication chronic vs. acute, vertebrogenic vs. non-vertebrogenic, with correct laterality and chronicity coding.

Missing Auth

Prior Authorization Not Obtained Before Acupuncture

Commercial payer requires prior authorization for acupuncture. Treatment delivered without auth. Retroactive denial for entire treatment course.

PMEx verifies prior authorization requirements before the first appointment and obtains authorization with clinical indication documentation. Every covered session has active authorization.

Dry Needling Confusion

Dry Needling and Acupuncture Billed Under Wrong Provider

PT performs dry needling, acupuncturist performs acupuncture on same patient same day. Claims intermixed under wrong provider. Payer denies as duplicate service.

PMEx separates dry needling (PT codes under PT NPI) and acupuncture (97810-97814 under acupuncturist NPI) correctly. No cross-billing or duplicate service denials.

Time Units Error

Acupuncture Timed Unit Calculation Under-Billed

15-minute add-on units (97811/97813) not applied when additional 15 minutes of needling time documented beyond initial unit. $25-$45 per session lost.

PMEx applies add-on unit codes when documented needling time exceeds initial unit thresholds capturing 97811 and 97813 on qualifying sessions.
